Health | Congressman Gregory Meeks Skip to main content 2310 Rayburn HOB, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-3461 Health Access to healthcare is a human right, not a privilege. Your zip code, color of your skin, or income should not determine the quality of care that you and your family receive. I have always been an advocate for access to quality healthcare in Congress and that starts with protecting access to the Affordable Care Act, to Medicare, and Medicaid–as well as supporting our local community health centers and hospital systems. We must also invest in mental health services and maternal care to close the gaps that have persisted for far too long. In our district, over 355,000 people are covered by Medicaid and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHP). It covers 32% of children under 19, 15% of adults 65+, and over 23,000 people with disabilities. In New York, Medicaid pays for the care of 64% of people in nursing homes. My constituents rely on these programs and others to survive. Any attack on these programs is an attack on the people of our district.    Under the Trump Administration, your access to healthcare is under threat. Extreme MAGA Republicans will stop at nothing to rob you of your access to care to pay for steep tax cuts for the nation’s ultra-wealthy.    I am committed to addressing health disparities and supporting legislation in Congress that safeguards access to quality healthcare for all Americans.   More on Health Rep. Technology | Congressman Gregory Meeks Skip to main content 2310 Rayburn HOB, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-3461 Technology Technology policy must be rooted in equity, innovation, and national strength. From how we connect to the internet to how we build the next generation of semiconductors; we must ensure that the digital economy works for everyone and not just a select few. That’s why I support policies that close the digital divide, invest in American innovation, protect our national security, and expand access to emerging technologies like artificial intelligence, clean tech, and advanced manufacturing. The future of our economy—and our democracy—depends on smart, inclusive technology policy that lifts up workers, families, and small businesses.   One of the most transformational investments we’ve made was through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act , which I proudly voted for. This law included $65 billion to expand broadband across the country. It also funded the Affordable Connectivity Program, which helps families pay for high-speed internet service – and I will keep advocating for the extension of this program.   I also proudly supported the CHIPS and Science Act , in order to help bring semiconductor manufacturing back to the U.S. For too long, we’ve depended on foreign supply chains for critical chips that power everything from smartphones to fighter jets. This law invested $52 billion in domestic chip production and boosts research and development so we can stay ahead in global innovation.   It also included major investments in STEM education and workforce development—especially for historically underrepresented communities—so that Black and Brown students and workers can help lead America’s tech future.   I will continue working in Congress to build a future where opportunity is truly accessible for every family in Southeast Queens and across the United States.   Issues Financial Services Foreign Affairs Guns and Justice Health Immigration Labor Technology

Immigration | Congressman Gregory Meeks Skip to main content 2310 Rayburn HOB, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-3461 Immigration As a Member of Congress from New York, I advocate for a just and humane immigration system that reflects the values of America and strengthens our communities. From Richmond Hill to Jamaica to Far Rockaway, immigrant communities are the heartbeat of New York’s Fifth Congressional District. Immigrants start businesses, serve in our military, care for our families, and contribute to every sector of our economy.   I support comprehensive immigration reform that includes a path to citizenship for Dreamers, Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders, farmworkers, and essential workers; stronger protections for asylum seekers and refugees; and modernized visa systems that reflect our economic needs and humanitarian values. I remain committed to pushing back against anti-immigrant rhetoric and policies that tear families apart and undermine America’s moral leadership.    I believe in securing our borders and that individuals who commit serious crimes—regardless of their immigration status—must be held accountable under the law. Public safety is a top priority, and there is no place in our communities for violent offenders. At the same time, I strongly oppose policies that demonize or target entire immigrant communities based on the actions of a few.    Most immigrants are law-abiding, hardworking members of society who contribute to our economy and enrich our neighborhoods. A just system must distinguish between those who pose a real threat and those seeking a better life—and focus enforcement accordingly, with fairness, due process, and respect for human dignity.   Let’s not forget this: Immigrants built New York City, and the United States of America!    More on Immigration Rep. Financial Services | Congressman Gregory Meeks Skip to main content 2310 Rayburn HOB, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-3461 Financial Services As a senior member of the House Financial Services Committee, I have long fought for a financial system that is fair, resilient, and inclusive. I am committed to ensuring all Americans, especially those in historically underserved communities, can access capital, credit, investment opportunities, and financial tools to build wealth. Growing up in public housing, I was inspired by parents that worked hard to ensure that their children had better opportunities than the ones they had. I believe that our communities thrive when everyone has access to wealth building opportunities that pave the way for future generations. Now, as a member of Congress, I bring that inspiration each day as I work to bridge the wealth gaps across our nation and to advocate for the underrepresented voice in financial services.   In Congress, I am focused on finding ways to:   Expand access to affordable housing and homeownership,   Strengthen Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs), Minority Deposit Institutions (MDIs) and community banks,   Promote diversity and inclusion in corporate governance and in the financial sector,   Champion reforms to safeguard consumers from predatory practices, improve financial literacy, and hold Wall Street accountable.    Ensure U.S. financial policy supports global economic stability and competitiveness.
